units.sanskrit: धृतराष्ट्रः उवाच अनुक्तम् यदि ते किम् चित् वाचा विदुर विद्यते तत् मे शुश्रूषवे ब्रूहि विचित्राणि हि भाषसे
units.english: individual exertion is futile.'" SECTION XLI (Sanat-sujata Parva) "Dhritarashtra said, 'If there is anything still left unsaid by thee, O Vidura, say it then, as I am ready to listen to thee.

units.sanskrit: विदुरः उवाच
units.english: The discourse is, indeed, charming.' "Vidura.

units.sanskrit: धृतराष्ट्रः उवाच किम् त्वम् न वेद तत् भूयः यत् मे ब्रूयात् सनातनः त्वम् एव विदुर ब्रूहि प्रज्ञा शेषः अस्ति चेद् तव
units.english: said, 'O Dhritarashtra, O thou of the Bharata race, that ancient and immortal Rishi Sanat-sujata who, leading a life perpetual celibacy, hath said that there is no Death,--that foremost of all intelligent persons,--will expound to thee all the doubts, in thy mind, both expressed and unexpressed.' "Dhritarashtra said, 'Dost thou not know what that immortal Rishi will say unto me? O Vidura, do thou say it, if indeed, thou hast that degree of wisdom.' "Vidura said, 'I am born in the Sudra order and, therefore, do not venture to say more than what I have already said.

units.sanskrit: कुमारस्य तु या बुद्धिः वेद ताम् शाश्वतीम् अहम्
units.english: The understanding, however, of that Rishi leading a life of celibacy, is regarded by me to be infinite.

units.sanskrit: ब्राह्मीम् हि योनिम् आपन्नः सु गुह्यम् अपि यः वदेत्
units.english: He that is a Brahmana by birth, by discoursing on even the profoundest mysteries, never incureth the censure of the gods.

units.sanskrit: न तेन गर्ह्यः देवानाम् तस्मात् एतत् ब्रवीमि ते धृतराष्ट्रः उवाच ब्रवीहि विदुर त्वम् मे पुराणम् तम् सनातनम्
units.english: It is for this alone that I do not discourse to thee, upon the subject.' "Dhritarashtra said, 'Tell me, O Vidura, how with this body of mine I can meet with that ancient and immortal one?' "Vaisampayana said, 'Then Vidura began to think of that Rishi of rigid vows.

units.sanskrit: चिन्तयाम् आस विदुरः तम् ऋषिम् संशित व्रतम् स च तत् चिन्तितम् ज्ञात्वा दर्शयाम् आस भारत
units.english: And knowing that he was thought of, the Rishi, O Bharata, showed himself there.

units.sanskrit: स च एनम् प्रतिजग्राह विधि दृष्टेन कर्मणा
units.english: Vidura then received him with the rites prescribed by ordinance.

units.sanskrit: सुख उपविष्टम् विश्रान्तम् अथ एनम् विदुरः अब्रवीत् भगवन् संशयः कः चित् धृतराष्ट्रस्य मानसे यः न शक्यः मया वक्तुम् तम् अस्मै वक्तुम् अर्हसि
units.english: And when, having rested a while, the Rishi was seated at his ease, Vidura addressed him, saying, 'O illustrious one, there is a doubt in Dhritarashtra's mind which is incapable of being explained away by me.

units.sanskrit: यम् श्रुत्वा अयम् मनुष्य इन्द्रः सुख दुःख अतिगः भवेत्
units.english: It behoveth thee, therefore, to expound it, so that listening to thy discourse, this chief of men may tide over all this sorrows, and to that gain and loss, what is agreeable and what disagreeable, decrepitude and death, fright and jealously, hunger and thirst, pride and prosperity, dislike, sleep, lust and wrath, and decrease and increase may all be borne by him!'" SECTION XLII "Vaisampayana said, 'Then the illustrious and wise king Dhritarashtra, having applauded the words spoken by Vidura, questioned Sanat-sujata in secret, desirous of obtaining the highest of all knowledge.

units.sanskrit: सनत्सुजात यदि इदम् शृणोमि मृत्युः हि न अस्ति इति तव उपदेशम्
units.english: And the king questioned the Rishi saying, 'O Sanat-sujata, I hear that thou art of the opinion that there is no Death.

units.sanskrit: देव असुराः हि आचरन् ब्रह्मचर्यम्
units.english: Again it is said that the gods and the Asuras, practise ascetic austerities in order to avoid death.

units.sanskrit: अमृत्यवे तत् कतरत् नु सत्यम् सनत्सुजातः उवाच
units.english: Of these two opinions, then, which is true?' "Sanat-sujata said, 'Some say, death is avertable by particular acts;

units.sanskrit: अमृत्युः कर्मणा के चित् मृत्युः न अस्ति इति च अपरे
units.english: others' opinion there is no death;

units.sanskrit: शृणु मे ब्रुवतः राजन् यथा एतत् मा विशङ्किथाः
units.english: Listen to me, O king, as I discourse to thee on this, so that thy doubts may be removed.

units.sanskrit: उभे सत्ये क्षत्रिय आदि अप्रवृत्ते
units.english: Know, O Kshatriya, that both of these are true.

units.sanskrit: मोहः मृत्युः संमतः यः कवीनाम्
units.english: The learned are of opinion that death results from ignorance.

units.sanskrit: प्रमादम् वै मृत्युम् अहम् ब्रवीमि सदा अप्रमादम् अमृत त्वम् ब्रवीमि
units.english: I say that ignorance is Death, and so the absence of ignorance (Knowledge) is immortality.

units.sanskrit: प्रमादात् वै असुराः पराभवन् अप्रमादात् ब्रह्म भूताः भवन्ति
units.english: It is from ignorance that the Asuras became subject to defeat and death, and it is from the absence of ignorance that the gods have attained the nature of Brahman.

units.sanskrit: न वै मृत्युः व्याघ्रः इव अत्ति जन्तून्
units.english: Death doth not devour creatures like a tiger;

units.sanskrit: न हि अस्य रूपम् उपलभ्यते ह
units.english: its form itself is unascertainable.

units.sanskrit: यमम् तु एके मृत्युम् अतस् अन्यम् आहुः
units.english: Besides this, some imagine Yama to be Death.

units.sanskrit: आत्म अवसन्नम् अमृतम् ब्रह्मचर्यम्
units.english: The pursuit of Brahman or self-knowledge is immortality.

units.sanskrit: पितृ लोके राज्यम् अनुशास्ति देवः शिवः शिवानाम् अशिवः अशिवानाम्
units.english: That (imaginary) god (Yama) holdeth his sway in the region of the Pitris, being the source of bliss to the virtuous and of woe to the sinful.

units.sanskrit: आस्यात् एष निःसरते नराणाम् क्रोधः प्रमादः मोह रूपः च मृत्युः
units.english: It is at his command that death in the form of wrath, ignorance, and covetousness, occurreth among men.

units.sanskrit: अहंगतेन एव चरन् विमार्गान्
units.english: Swayed by pride, men always walk in unrighteous path.

units.sanskrit: न च आत्मनः योगम् उपैति कः चित्
units.english: None amongst them succeeds in attaining to his real nature.

units.sanskrit: ते मोहिताः तद् वशे वर्तमाना
units.english: With their understanding clouded, and themselves swayed by there passions, they cast off their bodies and repeatedly fall into hell.

units.sanskrit: इतस् प्रेताः तत्र पुनर् पतन्ति
units.english: They are always followed by their senses.

units.sanskrit: अतस् मृत्युः मरण आख्याम् उपैति
units.english: It is for this that ignorance receives the name of death.

units.sanskrit: कर्म उदये कर्म फल अनुरागाः
units.english: Those men that desire the fruits of action when the time cometh for enjoying those fruits, proceed to heaven, casting off their bodies.

units.sanskrit: तत्र अनु यान्ति न तरन्ति मृत्युम् सत् अर्थ योगान् अवगमात् समन्तात्
units.english: Hence they cannot avoid death.

units.sanskrit: प्रवर्तते भोग योगेन देही
units.english: Embodied creatures, from inability to attain the knowledge of Brahman and from their connection with earthly enjoyments, are obliged to sojourn in a cycle of re-births, up and down and around, The natural inclination of man towards pursuits that are unreal is alone the cause of the senses being led to error.

units.sanskrit: मिथ्या अर्थ योगस्य गतिः हि नित्या मिथ्या अर्थ योग अभिहत अन्तरात्मा स्मरन् उपास्ते विषयान् समन्तात्
units.english: The soul that is constantly affected by the pursuit of objects that are unreal, remembering only that with which it is always engaged, adoreth only earthly enjoyments that surround it.

units.sanskrit: यः अभिध्यायन् उत्पतिष्णून् निहन्यात्
units.english: The desire of enjoyments first killeth men.

units.sanskrit: स वै मृत्युः मृत्युः इव अत्ति भूत्वा
units.english: They, however, that have conquered their souls, succeed by self-restraint, to escape death.

units.sanskrit: एवम् विद्वान् यः विनिहन्ति कामान्
units.english: Ignorance, assuming the form of Yama, cannot devour that learned man who controlled his desires in this manner.

units.sanskrit: काम अनुसारी पुरुषः कामान् अनु विनश्यति
units.english: That man who followeth his desires is destroyed along with his desires.

units.sanskrit: कामान् व्युदस्य धुनुते यत् किम् चित् पुरुषः रजः
units.english: He, however, that can renounce desire, can certainly drive away all kinds of woe.

units.sanskrit: तमः अप्रकाशः भूतानाम् नरकः अयम् प्रदृश्यते
units.english: Desire is, indeed, ignorance and darkness and hell in respect of all creatures, for swayed by it they lose their senses.

units.sanskrit: गृह्यन्तः इव धावन्ति गच्छन्तः श्वभ्रम् उन्मुखाः
units.english: As intoxicated persons in walking along a street reel towards ruts and holes, so men under the influence of desire, misled by deluding joys, run towards destruction.

units.sanskrit: अमूढ वृत्तेः पुरुषस्य इह कुर्यात् किम् वै मृत्युः तार्णः इव अस्य व्याघ्रः
units.english: What can death do to a person whose soul hath not been confounded or misled by desire? To him, death hath no terrors, like a tiger made of straw.

units.sanskrit: अ मन्यमानः क्षत्रिय किम् चित् अन्यन्
units.english: Therefore, O Kshatriya, if the existence of desire, which is ignorance, is to be destroyed, no wish, not even the slightest one, is either to be thought of or pursued.

units.sanskrit: क्रोधात् लोभात् मोह मय अन्तरात्मा स वै मृत्युः त्वद् शरीरे यः एषः
units.english: That soul, which is in thy body, associated as it is with wrath and covetousness and filled with ignorance, that is death.

units.sanskrit: एवम् मृत्युम् जायमानम् विदित्वा ज्ञाने तिष्ठन् न बिभेति इह मृत्योः विनश्यते विषये तस्य मृत्युः
units.english: Knowing that death arises in this way, he that relies on knowledge, entertaineth no fear of death.

units.sanskrit: मृत्योः यथा विषयम् प्राप्य मर्त्यः
units.english: Indeed, as the body is destroyed when brought under the influence of death, so death itself is destroyed when it comes under the influence of knowledge.' "Dhritarashtra said, 'The Vedas declare the emancipating capacity of those highly sacred and eternal regions, that are said to be obtainable by the regenerate classes by prayers and sacrifices.

units.sanskrit: एतत् विद्वान् न एति कथम् नु कर्म एवम् हि अ विद्वान् उपयाति तत्र तथा अर्थ जातम् च वदन्ति वेदाः
units.english: Knowing this, why should not a learned person have recourse to (religious) acts?'[3] "Sanat-sujata said, 'Indeed, he that is without knowledge proceedeth thither by the path indicated by thee, and the Vedas also declare that thither are both bliss and emancipation.

units.sanskrit: स न इह आयाति परम् परात्मा
units.english: But he that regardeth the material body to be self, if he succeeds in renouncing desire, at once attaineth emancipation (or Brahman).

units.sanskrit: किम् वा अस्य कार्यम् अथ वा सुखम् च सनत्सुजातः उवाच तत् मे विद्वन् ब्रूहि सर्वम् यथावत्
units.english: If, however, one seeketh emancipation without renouncing desire, one must have to proceed along the (prescribed) route of action, taking care to destroy the chances of his retracing the routes that he hath once passed over.'[4] "Dhritarashtra said, 'Who is it that urgeth that Unborn and Ancient One? If, again, it is He that is all this Universe in consequence of His having entered everything (without desire as He is) what can be His action, or his happiness? O learned sage, tell me all this truly.'[5] "Sanat-sujata said, 'There is great objection in completely identifying (as here) the two that are different Creatures always spring from the union of Conditions (with what in its essence is without Conditions).

units.sanskrit: हि अन् आदि योगेन भवन्ति नित्याः
units.english: This view doth not detract from the supremacy of the Unborn and the Ancient One.

units.sanskrit: अन् आदि योगेन भवन्ति पुंसः
units.english: As for men, they also originate in the union of Conditions.

units.sanskrit: यः एतत् वा भगवान् स नित्यः
units.english: All this that appears is nothing but that everlasting Supreme Soul.

units.sanskrit: विकार योगेन करोति विश्वम्
units.english: Indeed, the universe is created by the Supreme Soul itself undergoing transformations.

units.sanskrit: तथा च तद् शक्तिः इति स्म मन्यते
units.english: The Vedas to attribute this power (of self-transformation) to the Supreme Soul.

units.sanskrit: तथा अर्थ योगे च भवन्ति वेदाः धृतराष्ट्रः उवाच ये अस्मिन् धर्मान् न आचरन्ति इह के चिद्
units.english: For the identity, again, of the power and its possessor, both the Vedas and others are the authority.'[6] "Dhritarashtra said, 'In this world, some practise virtue, and some renounce action or Karma (adopting what is called Sannyasa Yoga).

units.sanskrit: उत अहो धर्मः प्रतिहन्ति पापम् सनत्सुजातः उवाच उभयम् एव तत्र उपभुज्यते फलम्
units.english: (Respecting those that practise virtue) I ask, is virtue competent to destroy vice, or is it itself destroyed by vice?' "Sanat-sujata said, 'The fruits of virtue and of (perfect) inaction are both serviceable in that respect (i.e., for procuring emancipation).

units.sanskrit: तस्मिन् स्थितः वा अपि उभयम् हि नित्यम्
units.english: Indeed, both are sure means for the attainment of emancipation.

units.sanskrit: ज्ञानेन विद्वान् प्रतिहन्ति सिद्धम्
units.english: The man, however, that is wise, achieveth success by knowledge (inaction).

units.sanskrit: तथा अन्यथा पुण्यम् उपैति देही
units.english: On the other hand, the materialist acquireth merit (by action) and (as the consequence thereof) emancipation.

units.sanskrit: तथागतम् पापम् उपैति सिद्धम्
units.english: He hath also (in course of his pursuit) to incur sin.

units.sanskrit: गत्वा उभयम् कर्मणा भुज्यते अस्थिरम्
units.english: Having obtained again fruits of both virtue and vice which are transitory, (heaven having its end as also hell in respect of the virtuous and the sinful), the man of action becometh once more addicted to action as the consequence of his own previous virtues and vices.

units.sanskrit: शुभस्य पापस्य स च अपि कर्मणा धर्मेण अधर्मम् प्रणुदति इह विद्वान्
units.english: The man of action, however, who possesseth intelligence, destroyeth his sins by his virtuous acts.

units.sanskrit: धर्मः बलीयान् इति तस्य विद्धि धृतराष्ट्रः उवाच यान् इमान् आहुः स्वस्य धर्मस्य लोकान्
units.english: Virtue, therefore, is strong, and hence the success of the man of action.' "Dhritarashtra said, 'Tell me, according to their gradation, of those eternal regions that are said to be attainable, as the fruits of their own virtuous acts, by regenerate persons, engaged in the practice of virtue.

units.sanskrit: तेषाम् परिक्रमान् कथयन्तः ततस् अन्यान्
units.english: Speak unto me of others' regions also of a similar kind.

units.sanskrit: येषाम् बले न विस्पर्धा बले बलवताम् इव
units.english: O learned sire, I do not wish to hear of actions (towards which man's heart naturally inclineth, however interdicted or sinful they may be).' "Sanat-sujata said, 'Those regenerate persons that take pride in their Yoga practices, like strong men in their own strength, departing hence, shine in the region of Brahman.

units.sanskrit: येषाम् धर्मे न च स्पर्धा तेषाम् तद् ज्ञान साधनम् ते ब्राह्मणाः इतस् मुक्ताः स्वर्गम् यान्ति त्रिविष्टपम्
units.english: Those regenerate persons that proudly exert in performing sacrifices and other Vedic rites, as the fruit of that knowledge which is theirs, in consequence of those acts, freed from this world, proceed to that region which is the abode of the deities.

units.sanskrit: तस्य सम्यक् समाचारम् आहुः वेद विदः जनाः
units.english: There are others, again, conversant with the Vedas, who are of opinion that the performance of the sacrifices and rites (ordained by the Vedas) is obligatory (their non-performance being sinful).

units.sanskrit: न एनम् मन्येत भूयिष्ठम् बाह्यम् आभ्यन्तरम् जनम्
units.english: Wedded to external forms, though seeking the development of the inner self (for they practise these rites for only virtue's sake and not for the accomplishment of particular aims), these persons should not be regarded very highly (although some respect should be theirs).

units.sanskrit: यत्र मन्येत भूयिष्ठम् प्रावृषि इव तृण उलपम् अन्नम् पानम् च ब्राह्मणः तत् जीवन् न अनुसंज्वरेत्
units.english: Wherever, again, food and drink worthy of a Brahmana are abundant, like grass and reeds in a spot during the rainy season, there should the Yogin seek for his livelihood (without afflicting the householder of scanty means);

units.sanskrit: यः वा अ कथयमानस्य आत्मानम् न अनुसंज्वरेत्
units.english: by no means should he afflict his own self by hunger and thirst.

units.sanskrit: एकः वै हि अन्तरात्मानम् ब्राह्मणः हन्तुम् अर्हति ब्रह्म स्वम् न उपभुञ्जेत् वा तत् अन्नम् संमतम् सताम्
units.english: The food offered by that person who is not pained at the sight of another disclosing his superiority, and who never eateth without offering the prescribed share to Brahmanas and guests, is approved by the righteous.

units.sanskrit: कुश वल्कल चेल आद्यम् ब्रह्म स्वम् योगिनः विदुः यथा स्वम् वान्तम् अश्नाति श्वा वै नित्यम् अभूतये एवम् ते वान्तम् अश्नन्ति स्व वीर्यस्य उपजीवनात्
units.english: As a dog oftentimes devoureth its own evacuations to its injury, so those Yogins devour their own vomit who procure their livelihood by disclosing their pre-eminence.

units.sanskrit: नित्यम् अज्ञात चर्या मे इति मन्येत ब्राह्मणः ज्ञातीनाम् तु वसन् मध्ये न एव विद्येत किम् चन
units.english: The wise know him for a Brahmana, who, living in the midst of kindred, wishes his religious practices to remain always unknown to them.

units.sanskrit: कः हि एवम् अन्तरात्मानम् ब्राह्मणः हन्तुम् अर्हति निर्लिङ्गम् अचलम् शुद्धम् सर्व द्वन्द्व विवर्जितम् तस्मात् हि किम् चित् क्षत्रिय ब्रह्म आवसति पश्यति
units.english: What other Brahmana deserveth to know the Supreme Soul, that is unconditioned, without attributes, unchangeable, one and alone, and without duality of any kind? In consequence of such practices, a Kshatriya can know the Supreme Soul and behold it in his own soul.

units.sanskrit: किम् तेन न कृतम् पापम् चोरेण आत्म अपहारिणा अश्रान्तः स्यात् अनादानात् संमतः निरुपद्रवः शिष्टः न शिष्टवत् स स्यात् ब्राह्मणः ब्रह्म विद् कविः
units.english: He that regardeth the Soul to be the acting and feeling Self,--what sins are not committed by that thief who robbeth the soul of its attributes? A Brahmana should be without exertion, should never accept gifts, should win the respect of the righteous, should be quiet, and though conversant with the Vedas should seem to be otherwise, for then only may he attain to knowledge and know Brahman.

units.sanskrit: अनाढ्याः मानुषे वित्ते आढ्याः वेदेषु ये द्विजाः ते दुर्धर्षाः दुष्प्रकम्प्याः विद्यात् तान् ब्रह्मणः तनुम्
units.english: They that are poor in earthly but rich in heavenly wealth and sacrifices, become unconquerable and fearless, and they should be regarded as embodiments of Brahman.

units.sanskrit: सर्वान् स्विष्टकृतः देवान् विद्यात् यः इह कः चन न समानः ब्राह्मणस्य यस्मिन् प्रयतते स्वयम्
units.english: That person even, in this world, who (by performing sacrifices) succeedeth in meeting with the gods that bestow all kinds of desirable objects (on performers of sacrifices), is not equal to him that knoweth Brahman for the performer of sacrifices hath to undergo exertions (while he that knoweth Brahman attaineth to Him without such exertions).

units.sanskrit: यम् अ प्रयतमानम् तु मानयन्ति स मानितः
units.english: He should never regard himself as honoured who is honoured by others.

units.sanskrit: न मान्यमानः मन्येत नाम अनात् अभिसंज्वरेत्
units.english: One should not, therefore, grieveth when one is not honoured by others.

units.sanskrit: लोकः स्वभाव वृत्तिः हि निमेष उन्मेष वत् सदा
units.english: People act according to their nature just as they open and shut their eyelids;

units.sanskrit: विद्वांसः मानयन्ति इह इति मन्येत मानितः
units.english: and it is only the learned that pay respect to others. The man that is respected should think so.

units.sanskrit: अधर्म विदुषः मूढाः लोक शास्त्र विशारदाः
units.english: They again, in this world, that are foolish, apt to sin, and adepts in deceit, never pay respect to those that are worthy of respect;

units.sanskrit: न मान्यम् मानयिष्यन्ति इति मन्येत् अ मानितः
units.english: on the other hand, they always show disrespect to such persons.

units.sanskrit: न वै मानम् च मौनम् च सहितौ चरतः सदा
units.english: The world's esteem and asceticism (practices of Mauna), can never exist together.

units.sanskrit: अयम् हि लोकः मानस्य असौ मानस्य तत् विदुः
units.english: Know that this world is for those that are candidates for esteem, while the other world is for those that are devoted to asceticism.

units.sanskrit: श्रीः सुखस्य इह संवासः सा च अपि परिपन्थिनी
units.english: Here, in this world, O Kshatriya, happiness (the world's esteem) resides in worldly prosperity.

units.sanskrit: ब्राह्मी सु दुर्लभा श्रीः हि प्रज्ञा हीनेन क्षत्रिय
units.english: Heavenly prosperity, on the other hand, is unattainable by one that is without true wisdom.

units.sanskrit: द्वाराणि तस्याः हि वदन्ति सन्तो बहु प्रकाराणि दुरावराणि
units.english: The righteous say that there are various kinds of gates, all difficult of being guarded, for giving access to the last kind of prosperity.

units.sanskrit: सत्य आर्जवे ह्रीः दम शौच विद्याः
units.english: These are truth, uprightness, modesty, self-control, purity of mind and conduct and knowledge (of the Vedas).

units.sanskrit: षष् मान मोह प्रतिबाधनानि धृतराष्ट्रः उवाच कस्य एष मौनः कतरत् नु मौनम्
units.english: These six are destructive of vanity and ignorance.'" SECTION XLIII "Dhritarashtra said, 'What is the object of asceticism (mauna)? Of the two kinds of mauna (viz., the restraining of speech and meditation), which is approved by thee? O learned one, tell me the true aspect of mauna.

units.sanskrit: मौनेन विद्वान् उत याति मौनम् सनत्सुजातः उवाच कथम् मुने मौनम् इह आचरन्ति
units.english: Can a person of learning attain to a state of quietude and emancipation (moksha) by that mauna? O Muni, how also is asceticism (mauna) to be practised here?' "Sanat-sujata said, 'Since the Supreme Soul cannot be penetrated by both the Vedas and the mind, it is for this that Soul itself is called mauna.

units.sanskrit: स तद् मय त्वेन विभाति राजन् धृतराष्ट्रः उवाच ऋचः यजूंषि अधीते यः सामवेदम् च यः द्विजः
units.english: That from which both the Vedic syllable Om and this one (ordinary sounds) have arisen, that One, O king, is displayed as the Word.' "Dhritarashtra said, 'Is he that knoweth both the Rig and the Yajus Vedas, is he that knoweth the Sama Veda, sullied by sins or not when he commiteth sins?' "Sanat-sujata said, 'I tell thee truly that the man that hath not restrained his senses is not rescued from his sinful acts by either the Sama or the Rig, or the Yajus Veda.

units.sanskrit: पापानि कुर्वन् पापेन लिप्यते न स लिप्यते
units.english: The Vedas never rescue from sin the deceitful person living by deceit.

units.sanskrit: धृतराष्ट्रः उवाच न चेद् वेदाः वेद विदम् शक्ताः त्रातुम् विचक्षण अथ कस्मात् प्रलापः अयम् ब्राह्मणानाम् सनातनः
units.english: On the other hand, like newfledged birds forsaking their nest, the Vedas forsake such a person at the end.' "Dhritarashtra said, 'O thou that hast restrained thy senses, if, indeed, the Vedas are not competent to rescue a person without the aid of virtue, whence then is this delusion of the Brahmanas that the Vedas are always destructive of sins?' "Sanat-sujata said, 'O magnanimous one, this universe hath sprung from that Supreme Soul by the union of Conditions respecting name, form, and other attributes.

units.sanskrit: तस्य एव नाम आदि विशेष रूपैः इदम् जगत् भाति महा अनुभाव निर्दिश्य सम्यक् प्रवदन्ति वेदाः
units.english: The Vedas also, pointing it out duly, declare the same, and inculcate that the Supreme Soul and the universe are different and not identical.

units.sanskrit: तद् अर्थम् उक्तम् तपः एतत् इज्या ताभ्याम् असौ पुण्यम् उपैति विद्वान्
units.english: It is for attaining to that Supreme Soul that asceticism and sacrifices are ordained, and it is by these two that the man of learning earneth virtue.

units.sanskrit: पुण्येन पापम् विनिहत्य पश्चात् संजायते ज्ञान विदीपित आत्मा
units.english: Destroying sin by virtue, his soul is enlightened by knowledge.

units.sanskrit: ज्ञानेन च आत्मानम् उपैति विद्वान्
units.english: The man of knowledge, by the aid of knowledge, attaineth to the Supreme Soul.

units.sanskrit: अथ अन्यथा वर्ग फल अनुकाङ्क्षी अस्मिन् कृतम् तत् परिगृह्य सर्वम् अमुत्र भुङ्क्ते पुनर् एति मार्गम्
units.english: Otherwise, he that coveteth the four objects of human pursuit, taking with him all that he doth here, enjoyeth their fruits hereafter, and (as those fruits) are not everlasting cometh back to the region of action (when the enjoyment is over).

units.sanskrit: एतत् समृद्धम् अत्यृद्धम् तपः भवति केवलम् अस्मिन् लोके तपः तप्तम् फलम् अन्यत्र दृश्यते
units.english: Indeed, the fruits of ascetic austerities performed in this world have to be enjoyed in the other world (as regards those persons who have not obtained the mastery of their souls).

units.sanskrit: ब्राह्मणानाम् इमे लोकाः ऋद्धे तपसि संयताः धृतराष्ट्रः उवाच कथम् समृद्धम् अपि ऋद्धम् तपः भवति केवलम्
units.english: As regards those Brahmanas employed in ascetic practices (who have the mastery of their souls), even these regions are capable of yielding fruits.' "Dhritarashtra said, 'O Sanat-sujata, how can ascetic austerities which are all of the same kind, be sometimes successful and sometimes unsuccessful? Tell us this in order that we may know it!' "Sanat-sujata said, 'That asceticism which is not stained by (desire and other) faults is said to be capable of procuring emancipation, and is, therefore, successful, while the asceticism that is stained by vanity and want of true devotion is regarded unsuccessful.

units.sanskrit: एतत् समृद्धम् अपि ऋद्धम् तपः भवति न अन्यथा तपः मूलम् इदम् सर्वम् यत् माम् पृच्छसि क्षत्रिय
units.english: All thy enquiries, O Kshatriya, touch the very root of asceticism.

units.sanskrit: धृतराष्ट्रः उवाच तपसा वेद विद्वांसः परम् तु अमृतम् आप्नुयुः
units.english: It is by asceticism that they that are learned, know Brahman and win immortality!' "Dhritarashtra said, 'I have listened to what thou hast said about asceticism unstained by faults, and by which I have succeeded in knowing an eternal mystery.

units.sanskrit: सनत्सुजातः उवाच क्रोध आदयः द्वादश यस्य दोषाः तथा नृशंस आदि षट् अत्र राजन्
units.english: Tell me now, O Sanat-sujata, about asceticism that is stained by faults!' "Sanat-sujata said, 'O king, the twelve, including anger, as also the thirteen kinds of wickedness, are the faults of asceticism that is stained.

units.sanskrit: क्रोधः कामः लोभ मोहौ विवित्सा कृपा असूया मान शोकौ स्पृहा च ईर्ष्या जुगुप्सा च मनुष्य दोषा
units.english: Anger, lust, avarice, ignorance of right and wrong, discontent, cruelty, malice, vanity, grief, love of pleasure, envy, and speaking ill of others, are generally the faults of human beings.

units.sanskrit: वर्ज्याः सदा द्वादशा एते नरेण
units.english: These twelve should always be avoided by men.

units.sanskrit: एकैकम् एते राज इन्द्र मनुष्यान् पर्युपासते
units.english: Any one amongst these can singly effect the destruction of men, O bull among men.

units.sanskrit: लिप्समानः अन्तरम् तेषाम् मृगाणाम् इव लुब्धकः
units.english: Indeed, every one of these wait for opportunity in respect of men, like a hunter expectant of opportunities in respect of deer.

units.sanskrit: एते प्राप्ताः षट् नरान् पाप धर्मान् प्रकुर्वते न उत सन्तः सु दुर्गे संभोग संविद् द्विषम् एधमानः
units.english: Assertion of one's own superiority, desire of enjoying others' wives, humiliating others from excess of pride, wrathfulness, fickleness, and refusing to maintain those worthy of being maintained, these six acts of wickedness are always practised by sinful men defying all dangers here and hereafter.

units.sanskrit: दत्त अनुतापी कृपणः अ बलीयान् वर्ग प्रशंसी वनितासु द्वेष्टा एते अपरे सप्त नृशंस धर्माः
units.english: He that regards the gratification of lust to be one of life's aims, he that is exceedingly proud, he that grieves having given away, he that never spends money, he that persecutes his subjects by exacting hateful taxes, he that delights in the humiliation of others, and he that hates his own wives,--these seven are others that are also called wicked.

units.sanskrit: धर्मः च सत्यम् च दमः तपः च अमात्सर्यम् ह्रीः तितिक्षा अनसूया यज्ञः च दानम् च धृतिः श्रुतम् च
units.english: Righteousness, truth (abstention from injury and truthfulness of speech), self-restraint, asceticism, delight in the happiness of others, modesty, forbearance, love of others, sacrifices, gifts, perseverance, knowledge of the scriptures,--these twelve constitute the practices of Brahmanas.

units.sanskrit: यः तु एतेभ्यः प्रवसेत् द्वादशेभ्यः सर्वाम् अपि इमाम् पृथिवीम् प्रशिष्यात्
units.english: He that succeeds in acquiring these twelve, becomes competent to sway the entire earth.

units.sanskrit: त्रिभिः द्वाभ्याम् एकतस् वा विशिष्टः
units.english: He that is endued with three, two, or even one, of these, should be regarded of heavenly prosperity.

units.sanskrit: दमः त्यागः अप्रमादः च एतेषु अमृतम् आहितम्
units.english: Self-restraint, renunciation, and knowledge of Self,--in these are emancipation.

units.sanskrit: तानि सत्य मुखानि आहुः ब्राह्मणाः ये मनीषिणः
units.english: Those Brahmanas that are endued with wisdom, say, that these are attributes in which truth predominates.

units.sanskrit: दमः अष्टादश दोषः स्यात् प्रतिकूलम् कृत अकृते
units.english: Self-restraint is constituted by eighteen virtues.

units.sanskrit: अनृतम् च अभ्यसूया च काम अर्थौ च तथा स्पृहा क्रोधः शोकः तथा तृष्णा लोभः पैशुन्यम् एव च मत्सरः च विवित्सा च परितापः तथा रतिः
units.english: Breaches and non-observance of ordained acts and omissions, falsehood, malice, lust, wealth, love of (sensual) pleasure, anger, grief, thirst, avarice, deceit, joy in the misery of others, envy, injuring others, regret, aversion from pious acts, forgetfulness of duty, calumniating others, and vanity-he that is freed from these (eighteen) vices;

units.sanskrit: एतैः विमुक्तः दोषैः यः स दमः सद्भिः उच्यते
units.english: is said by the righteous to be self-restrained.

units.sanskrit: मदः अष्टादश दोषः स्यात् त्यागः भवति षड्गुणः
units.english: The eighteen faults (that have been enumerated) constitute what is called mada or pride. Renunciation is of six kinds.

units.sanskrit: विपर्ययाः स्मृताः एते मद दोषाः उदाहृताः
units.english: The reverse of those six again are faults called mada. (The faults, therefore, that go by the name of mada are eighteen and six).

units.sanskrit: श्रेयान् तु षड्विधः त्यागः तृतीयः तत्र दुष्करः
units.english: The six kinds of renunciation are all commendable. The third only is difficult of practice, but by that all sorrow is overcome.

units.sanskrit: तेन दुःखम् तरन्ति एव तस्मिन् त्यक्ते जितम् भवेत्
units.english: Indeed, if that kind of renunciation be accomplished in practice, he that accomplishes it overcomes all the pairs of contraries in the world.

units.sanskrit: श्रेयान् तु षड्विधः त्यागः प्रियम् प्राप्य न हृष्यति
units.english: 'The six kinds of renunciation are all commendable. They are these: The first is never experiencing joy on occasions of prosperity.

units.sanskrit: अप्रिये तु समुत्पन्ने व्यथाम् जातु न च अर्च्छति
units.english: Or, when anything disagreeable happens, one feeleth no pain.

units.sanskrit: इष्टान् दारान् च पुत्रान् च न च अन्यम् यत् वचः भवेत्
units.english: The fifth kind of renunciation consists in not soliciting even one's sons, wives, and others that may all be very dear.

units.sanskrit: अर्हते याचमानाय प्रदेयम् तत् वचः भवेत्
units.english: The sixth kind consists in giving away to a deserving person who solicits, which act of gifts is always productive of merit.

units.sanskrit: इष्टापूर्तम् द्वितीयम् स्यात् नित्यम् वैराग्य योगतः
units.english: By these again, one acquires the knowledge of Self.

units.sanskrit: अप्रमादी भवेत् एतैः स च अपि अष्टगुणः महान्
units.english: As regards this last attribute, it involves eight qualities.

units.sanskrit: सत्यम् ध्यानम् समाधानम् चोद्यम् वैराग्यम् एव च अस्तेयः ब्रह्मचर्यम् च तथा असंग्रहः एव च
units.english: These are truth, meditation, distinction of subject and object, capacity for drawing inferences, withdrawal from the world, never taking what belongeth to others, the practices of Brahmacharya vows (abstinence), and non-acceptance (of gifts).

units.sanskrit: एवम् दोषाः मदस्य उक्ताः तान् दोषान् परिवर्जयेत्
units.english: These faults should be avoided.

units.sanskrit: दोषत्यागः अप्रमादः स्यात् स च अपि अष्टगुणः मतः
units.english: And as, self-Knowledge hath eight virtues, so the want of it hath eight faults.

units.sanskrit: सत्य आत्मा भव राज इन्द्र सत्ये लोकाः प्रतिष्ठिताः
units.english: O king, let thy soul be devoted to truth; all the worlds are established on truth;

units.sanskrit: निवृत्तेन एव दोषेण तपः व्रतम् इह आचरेत्
units.english: Avoiding (these) faults, one should practise asceticism here.

units.sanskrit: एतत् धातृ कृतम् वृत्तम् सत्यम् एव सताम् व्रतम्
units.english: The Ordainer hath ordained that truth alone should be the vow of the righteous.

units.sanskrit: एतत् पाप हरम् शुद्धम् जन्म मृत्यु जरा अपहम् धृतराष्ट्रः उवाच आख्यान पञ्चमैः वेदैः भूयिष्ठम् कथ्यते जनः
units.english: Asceticism, that is dissociated from these faults and endued with these virtues, becomes the source of great prosperity, I have now briefly told these about that sin-destroying and sacred subject which thou hadst asked me and which is capable of liberating a person from birth, death, and decrepitude.' "Dhritarashtra said, 'With Akhyana (Puranas) as their fifth, the Vedas declare the Supreme Soul to be this universe consisting of mobile and immobile things.

units.sanskrit: तथा एव अन्ये चतुर् वेदाः त्रि वेदाः च तथा अपरे
units.english: and others three;

units.sanskrit: द्वि वेदाः च एक वेदाः च अनृचः च तथा अपरे
units.english: and others only one;

units.sanskrit: तेषाम् तु कतमः स स्यात् यम् अहम् वेद ब्राह्मणम् सनत्सुजातः उवाच
units.english: Amongst these, which should I know to be really possessed of the knowledge of Brahman.' "Sanat-sujata, 'There is but one Brahman which is Truth's self.

units.sanskrit: एकस्य वेदस्य अज्ञानात् वेदाः ते बहवः अभवन्
units.english: It is from ignorance of that One, that god-heads have been conceived to be diverse.

units.sanskrit: सत्यस्य एकस्य राज इन्द्र सत्ये कः चित् अवस्थितः एवम् वेदम् अन् उत्साद्य प्रज्ञाम् महति कुर्वते दानम् अध्ययनम् यज्ञः लोभात् एतत् प्रवर्तते
units.english: But who is there, O king, that hath attained to Truth's self or Brahman? Man regardeth himself wise without knowing that One Object of knowledge, and from desire of happiness is engaged in study and the practices of charity and sacrifices.

units.sanskrit: सत्यात् प्रच्यवमानानाम् संकल्पः वितथः भवेत् ततस् यज्ञः प्रतायेत सत्यस्य एव अवधारणात्
units.english: They have deviated from Truth (Brahman) and entertain purposes corresponding (with their state) and hence relying on the truth of Vedic texts thereof perform sacrifices.

units.sanskrit: मनसा अन्यस्य भवति वाचा अन्यस्य उत कर्मणा
units.english: Some perform (or attain the object of) sacrifices by the mind (meditation), some by words (recitation of particular prayers, or Yapa); and some by acts (actual consummation of the Yatishtoma and other costly rites).

units.sanskrit: संकल्प सिद्धः पुरुषः संकल्पान् अधितिष्ठति
units.english: The person, however, who seeketh Brahman through Truth, obtaineth his desired objects at home.

units.sanskrit: अ नैभृत्येन वै तस्य दीक्षित व्रतम् आचरेत्
units.english: When however, one's purposes become abortive (through absence of knowledge of Self), one should adopt vows of silence and such like, called Dikshavrata.

units.sanskrit: नाम एतत् धातु निर्वृत्तम् सत्यम् एव सताम् परम्
units.english: As regards those that have knowledge of Self, with them Truth is the highest object of pursuit.' 'The fruits of knowledge are visible;

units.sanskrit: ज्ञानम् वै नाम प्रत्यक्षम् परोक्षम् जायते तपः
units.english: asceticism yieldeth fruits hereafter.

units.sanskrit: विद्यात् बहु पठन्तम् तु बहु पाठी इति ब्राह्मणम्
units.english: A Brahmana who (without knowledge and asceticism) hath only read much should only be known as a great reader.

units.sanskrit: तस्मात् क्षत्रिय मा मंस्थाः जल्पितेन एव ब्राह्मणम्
units.english: Therefore, O Kshatriya, never think that one can be a Brahman (Brahman-knowing) by only reading the scriptures.

units.sanskrit: यः एव सत्यात् न अपैति स ज्ञेयः ब्राह्मणः त्वया
units.english: He, on the other hand, should be known by thee to be possessed of the knowledge of the Brahman who doth not deviate from Truth.

units.sanskrit: छन्दांसि नाम द्विपदाम् वरिष्ठ
units.english: O Kshatriya, the verses that were recited by Atharvan to a conclave of great sages, in days of old, are known by the name of Chhandas.

units.sanskrit: छन्दः विदः तेन च तान् अधीत्य गताः हि वेदस्य न वेद्यम् आर्याः
units.english: They are not be regarded as acquainted with the Chhandas who have only read through the Vedas, without having attained to the knowledge of Him who is known through the Vedas.

units.sanskrit: न वेदानाम् वेदिता कः चित् अस्ति
units.english: They cannot be regarded as acquainted with the Chhandas who are acquainted only with the modes of sacrifice enjoined in the Vedas.

units.sanskrit: वेद्येन वेदम् न विदुः न वेद्यम्
units.english: On the other hand, having waited upon those that are acquainted with the Vedas, have not the righteous attained to the Object that is knowable by the Vedas? There is none who hath truly caught the sense of the Vedas or there may be some who have, O king, caught the sense.

units.sanskrit: यः वेद वेदम् स च वेद वेद्यम्
units.english: He that hath only read the Vedas, doth not know the Object knowable by them.

units.sanskrit: यः वेद वेद्यम् न स वेद सत्यम् यः वेद वेदान् स च वेद वेद्यम्
units.english: He, however, that is established in Truth, know the Object knowable by the Vedas.

units.sanskrit: न तम् विदुः वेद विदः न वेदाः
units.english: Amongst those faculties which lead to perception of the body as the acting agent, there is none by which true knowledge may be acquired.

units.sanskrit: तथा अपि वेदेन विदन्ति वेदम्
units.english: Indeed, he that knoweth Self also knoweth what is Not-self.

units.sanskrit: तस्मिन् हि सत्ये परमात्मनः अर्थे
units.english: He, on the other hand, that knoweth only what is Not-self, doth not know Truth.

units.sanskrit: छन्दः विदः ते ये उ तान् अधीत्य
units.english: He, again, that knoweth the proofs, knoweth also that which is sought to be proved.

units.sanskrit: न वेदानाम् वेदिता कः चित् अस्ति कः चित् वेदान् बुध्यते वा अपि राजन् यः वेद वेदान् न स वेद वेद्यम्
units.english: But what that Object in its nature is (which is sought to be proved) is not known to either the Vedas or those that are acquainted with the Vedas.

units.sanskrit: सत्ये स्थितः यः तु स वेद वेद्यम्
units.english: For all that, however, those Brahmanas that are (truly) acquainted with the Vedas succeed in obtaining a knowledge of the Object knowable (by the Vedas) through the Vedas.

units.sanskrit: अभिजानामि ब्राह्मणम् आख्यातारम् विचक्षणम् एवम् यः हि विजानाति स जानाति परम् हि तत् परम् हि तत् परम् ब्रह्म जानाति एव च ब्राह्मणः
units.english: I know him to be a Brahmana (possessing a knowledge of Brahman) who expoundeth the doubts of others, having himself mastered all his own doubts, and who is possessed of the knowledge of Self.

units.sanskrit: तस्य पर्येषणम् गच्छेत् प्राचीनम् न उत दक्षिणम् न अर्वाचीनम् कुतस् तिर्यक् न आदिशम् तु कथम् चन
units.english: One cannot find what the Soul is by seeking in the East, the South, the West, the North, or in the subsidiary directions or horizontally.

units.sanskrit: अभ्यावर्तेत ब्रह्मा अस्य अन्तरात्मनि वै श्रितम्
units.english: Completely restraining all thy senses and thy mind also seek thou that Brahman which is known to reside in thy own Soul.

units.sanskrit: मौनात् हि स मुनिः भवति न आरण्य वसनात् मुनिः
units.english: He is not a Muni who practiseth only Yoga-meditation; nor he who liveth only in the woods (having retired from the world).

units.sanskrit: अक्षरम् तत् तु यः वेद स मुनिः श्रेष्ठः उच्यते
units.english: He, however, is a Muni and is superior to all who knoweth his own nature.

units.sanskrit: सर्व अर्थानाम् व्याकरणात् वैयाकरणः उच्यते
units.english: In consequence of one's being able to expound every object (Vyakarana), one is said to be endued with universal knowledge (Vaiyakarana);

units.sanskrit: तत् मूलतः व्याकरणम् व्याकरोति इति तत् तथा
units.english: and, indeed, the science itself is called Vyakarana owing to its being able to expound every object to its very root (which is Brahman).

units.sanskrit: प्रत्यक्ष दर्शी लोकानाम् सर्व दर्शी भवेत् नरः
units.english: The man who beholdeth all the regions as present before his eyes, is said to be possessed of universal knowledge.

units.sanskrit: सत्ये वै ब्राह्मणः तिष्ठन् ब्रह्म पश्यति क्षत्रिय
units.english: He that stayeth in Truth and knoweth Brahman is said to be a Brahmana, and a Brahmana, possesseth universal knowledge.

units.sanskrit: ज्ञान आदिषु स्थितः अपि एवम् क्षत्रिय ब्रह्म पश्यति
units.english: A Kshatriya also, that practises such virtues, may behold Brahman.

units.sanskrit: वेदानाम् च आनुपूर्व्येण एतत् विद्वन् ब्रवीमि ते धृतराष्ट्रः उवाच सनत्सुजात यत् इमाम् परार्थाम्
units.english: Knowing it for certain, I tell thee this.'" SECTION XLIV "Dhritarashtra said, 'Excellent, O Sanat-sujata, as this thy discourse is, treating of the attainment of Brahman and the origin of the universe.

units.sanskrit: सनत्सुजातः उवाच न एतत् ब्रह्म त्वरमाणेन लभ्यम् यत् माम् पृच्छसि अभिहृष्यसि अतीव
units.english: I pray thee, O celebrated Rishi, to go on telling me words such as these, that are unconnected with objects of worldly desire and are, therefore, rare among men.' "Sanat-sujata said, 'That Brahman about which thou askest me with such joy is not to be attained soon.

units.sanskrit: बुद्धौ प्रलीने मनसि प्रचिन्त्या
units.english: After (the senses have been restrained and) the will hath been merged in the pure intellect, the state that succeeds in one of utter absence of worldly thought.

units.sanskrit: विद्या हि सा ब्रह्मचर्येण लभ्या
units.english: Even that is knowledge (leading to the attainment of Brahman).

units.sanskrit: बुद्ध्या च तेषाम् ब्रह्मचर्येण सिद्धाम् धृतराष्ट्रः उवाच
units.english: It is attainable only by practising Brahmacharya.' "Dhritarashtra said, 'Thou sayest that the knowledge of Brahman dwelleth of itself in the mind, being only discovered by Brahmacharya;

units.sanskrit: अव्यक्त विद्याम् इति यत् सनातनीम्
units.english: How then is the immortality associated with the attainment of Brahman?' "Sanat-sujata said, 'Though residing in and inherent to the mind, the knowledge of Brahman is still unmanifest.

units.sanskrit: ब्रवीषि त्वम् ब्रह्मचर्येण सिद्धाम्
units.english: It is by the aid of the pure intellect and Brahmacharya that, that knowledge is made manifest.

units.sanskrit: याम् प्राप्य एताम् मर्त्य लोकम् त्यजन्ति
units.english: Indeed, having attained to that knowledge, Yogins forsake this world.

units.sanskrit: या वै विद्या गुरु वृद्धेषु नित्या
units.english: It is always to be found among eminent preceptors.

units.sanskrit: धृतराष्ट्रः उवाच ब्रह्मचर्येण या विद्या शक्या वेदितुम् अञ्जसा तत् कथम् ब्रह्मचर्यम् स्यात् एतत् विद्वन् ब्रवीहि मे
units.english: I shall now discourse to thee on that knowledge.' "Dhritarashtra said, 'What should be the nature of that Brahmacharya by which the knowledge of Brahman might be attained without much difficulty? O regenerate one, tell me this.' "Sanat-sujata said, 'They, who, residing in the abodes of their preceptors and winning their good will and friendship, practise Brahmacharya austerities, become even in this world the embodiments of Brahman and casting off their bodies are united with the Supreme Soul.

units.sanskrit: ये अस्मिन् लोके विजयन्ति इह कामान् ब्राह्मीम् स्थितिम् अनुतितिक्षमाणाः ते आत्मानम् निर्हरन्ति इह देहान्
units.english: They that in this world desirous of obtaining the state of Brahman, subdue all desires, and endued as they are with righteousness, they succeed in dissociating the Soul from the body like a blade projected from a clump of heath.

units.sanskrit: शरीरम् एतौ कुरुतः पिता माता च भारत
units.english: The body, O Bharata, is created by these, viz., the father and the mother;

units.sanskrit: आचार्य शास्ता या जातिः सा सत्या सा अजरा अमरा आचार्यतः तु यत् जन्म तत् सत्यम् वै तथा अमृतम्
units.english: the (new) birth, however, that is due to the preceptor's instructions is sacred, free from decrepitude, and immortal.

units.sanskrit: तम् मन्येत पितरम् मातरम् च
units.english: Discoursing upon Brahman and granting immortality, he who wraps all persons with (the mantle of) truth, should be regarded as father and mother;

units.sanskrit: तस्मै न द्रुह्येत् कृतम् अस्य जानन्
units.english: and bearing in mind the good he does, one should never do him any injury.

units.sanskrit: गुरुम् शिष्यः नित्यम् अभिमन्यमानः स्वाध्यायम् इच्छेत् शुचिः अप्रमत्तः
units.english: A disciple must habitually salute his preceptor with respect, and with purity (of body and mind) and well-directed attention, he must betake to study.

units.sanskrit: मानम् न कुर्यात् न दधीत रोषम्
units.english: He must not consider any service as mean, and must not harbour anger.

units.sanskrit: एष प्रथमः ब्रह्मचर्यस्य पादः
units.english: Even this is the first step of Brahmacharya.

units.sanskrit: शिष्य वृत्ति क्रमेण एव विद्याम् आप्नोति यः शुचिः ब्रह्मचर्य व्रतस्य अस्य प्रथमः पादः उच्यते
units.english: The practices of that disciple who acquires knowledge by observing the duties ordained for one of his class are regarded also as the first step of Brahmacharya.

units.sanskrit: आचार्यस्य प्रियम् कुर्यात् प्राणैः अपि धनैः अपि
units.english: A disciple should, with his very life and all his possessions, in thought, word and deed, do all that is agreeable to the preceptor.

units.sanskrit: कर्मणा मनसा वाचा द्वितीयः पादः उच्यते
units.english: This is regarded as the second step of Brahmacharya.

units.sanskrit: समा गुरौ यथा वृत्तिः गुरु पत्न्याम् तथा भवेत्
units.english: He should behave towards his preceptor's wife and son also in the same way as towards his preceptor himself.

units.sanskrit: यथा उक्त कारी प्रिय कृत् तृतीयः पादः उच्यते
units.english: This also is regarded as the second step of Brahmacharya.

units.sanskrit: आचार्येण आत्म कृतम् विजानञ् ज्ञात्वा च अर्थम् भावितः अस्मि इति अनेन यत् मन्यते तम् प्रति हृष्ट बुद्धिः
units.english: Bearing well in mind what has been done to him by the preceptor, and understanding also its object, the disciple should, with a delighted heart think,--I have been taught and made great by him.

units.sanskrit: स वै तृतीयः ब्रह्मचर्यस्य पादः
units.english: This is the third step of Brahmacharya.

units.sanskrit: न आचार्याय इह उपकृत्वा प्रवादम् प्राज्ञः कुर्वीत न एतत् अहम् करोमि
units.english: Without requiring the preceptor by payment of the final gift, a wise disciple must not betake to another mode of life;

units.sanskrit: इति इव मन्येत न भाषयेत
units.english: nor should he say or even think of in his mind,--I make this gift.

units.sanskrit: स वै चतुर्थः ब्रह्मचर्यस्य पादः एवम् वसन्तम् यत् उपप्लवेत् हि
units.english: This is the fourth step of Brahmacharya.

units.sanskrit: स वै चतुर्थः ब्रह्मचर्यस्य पादः कालेन पादम् लभते तथार्थम्
units.english: He attaineth the first step of (knowledge of Brahman which is) the object of Brahmacharya by aid of time;

units.sanskrit: ततस् च पादम् गुरु योगतः च
units.english: the second step, through the preceptor's prelections;

units.sanskrit: छास्त्रेण पादम् च ततस् अभियाति
units.english: and finally, the fourth, by discussion.

units.sanskrit: ज्ञान आदयः द्वादश यस्य रूपम् अन्यानि च अङ्गानि तथा बलम् च आचार्य योगे फलति इति च आहुः
units.english: The learned have said that Brahmacharya is constituted by the twelve virtues, the Yoga-practices are called its Angas, and perseverance in Yoga-meditation called is its Valam and one is crowned with success in this in consequence of the preceptor's aid and the understanding of the sense of the Vedas.

units.sanskrit: एवम् वसन्तम् यत् उपप्लवेत् धनम् आचार्याय तत् अनुप्रयच्छेत्
units.english: Whatever wealth a disciple, thus engaged, may earn, should all be given to the preceptor.

units.sanskrit: सताम् वृत्तिम् बहु गुणाम् एवम् एति
units.english: It is thus that the preceptor obtaineth his highly praise-worthy livelihood.

units.sanskrit: गुरोः पुत्रे भवति च वृत्तिः एषा
units.english: And thus also should the disciple behave towards the preceptor's son.

units.sanskrit: एवम् वसन् सर्वतस् वर्धति इह बहून् पुत्रान् लभते च प्रतिष्ठाम्
units.english: Thus stationed (in Brahmacharya), the disciple thriveth by all means in this world and obtaineth numerous progeny and fame.

units.sanskrit: वर्षन्ति च अस्मै प्रदिशः दिशः च
units.english: Men also from all directions shower wealth upon him;

units.sanskrit: वसन्ति अस्मिन् ब्रह्मचर्ये जनाः च
units.english: and many people come to his abode for practising Brahmacharya.

units.sanskrit: एतेन ब्रह्मचर्येण देवाः देव त्वम् आप्नुवन् ऋषयः च महाभागाः ब्रह्म लोकम् मनीषिणः
units.english: It is through Brahmacharya of this kind that the celestials attained to their divinity, and sages, highly blessed and of great wisdom, have obtained the region of Brahman.

units.sanskrit: गन्धर्वाणाम् अनेन एव रूपम् अप्सरसाम् अभूत् एतेन ब्रह्मचर्येण सूर्यः अह्नाय जायते
units.english: It is by this that the Gandharvas and the Apsaras acquired such personal beauty, and it is through Brahmacharya that Surya riseth to make the day.

units.sanskrit: यः आशयेत् पाटयेत् च अपि राजन् सर्वम् शरीरम् तपसा तप्यमानः एतेन असौ बाल्यम् अत्येति विद्वान्
units.english: He, O king, who devoted to the practice of ascetic austerities, betaketh himself to Brahmacharya in its entirety and thereby purifieth his body, is truly wise, for by this he becometh like a child (free from all evil passions) and triumpheth over death at last.

units.sanskrit: अन्तवन्तः क्षत्रिय ते जयन्ति लोकान् जनाः कर्मणा निर्मितेन
units.english: Men, O Kshatriya, by work, however, pure, obtain only worlds that are perishable;

units.sanskrit: ब्रह्मा एव विद्वान् तेन अभ्येति सर्वम्
units.english: he, however, that is blessed with Knowledge, attaineth, by the aid of that Knowledge, to Brahman which is everlasting.

units.sanskrit: न अन्यः पन्थाः अयनाय विद्यते
units.english: There is no other path (than Knowledge or the attainment of Brahman) leading to emancipation.

units.sanskrit: धृतराष्ट्रः उवाच
units.english: "Dhritarashtra said, 'The existence of Brahman, thou sayest, a wise man perceiveth in his own soul.

units.sanskrit: आभाति शुक्लम् इव लोहितम् इव अथ उ कृष्णम् अथ अञ्जनम् काद्रवम् वा तत् ब्राह्मणः पश्यति यः अत्र विद्वान्
units.english: Now, is Brahman white, or red, or black or blue, or purple? Tell me what is the true form and colour of the Omnipresent and Eternal Brahman?' "Sanat-sujata said, 'Indeed, Brahman as (perceived) may appear as white, red, black, brown, or bright.

units.sanskrit: न च अभ्रेषु दृश्यते रूपम् अस्य न च अपि वायौ न च देवतासु न तत् चन्द्रे दृश्यते न उत सूर्ये
units.english: But neither on the earth, nor in the sky, nor in the water of the ocean, is there anything like it, Neither in the stars, nor in lightning, nor in the clouds, is its form to be seen, nor is it visible in the atmosphere, nor in the deities, nor in the moon, nor in the sun.

units.sanskrit: न एव ऋक्षु तत् न यजुःषु न अपि अथर्वसु न च एव दृश्यति अमलेषु सामसु
units.english: Neither in the Riks, nor among the Yajus, nor among the Atharvans, nor in the pure Samans, it is to be found.

units.sanskrit: रथंतरे बार्हते च अपि राजन् महाव्रते न एव दृश्येत् ध्रुवम् तत्
units.english: Verily, O king, it is not to be found in Rathantara or Varhadratha, nor in great sacrifices.

units.sanskrit: तत् अन्तकः अपि एति विनाश काले
units.english: Incapable of being compassed and lying beyond the reach of the limited intellect, even the universal Destroyer, after the Dissolution, is himself lost in it.

units.sanskrit: अणीय रूपम् क्षुर धारया तन् महत् च रूपम् तु अपि पर्वतेभ्यः
units.english: Incapable of being gazed at, it is subtle as the edge of the razor, and grosser than mountains.

units.sanskrit: सा प्रतिष्ठा तत् अमृतम् लोकाः तत् ब्रह्म तत् यशः
units.english: it is unchangeable; it is this visible universe (omnipresent);

units.sanskrit: भूतानि जज्ञिरे तस्मात् प्रलयम् यान्ति तत्र च
units.english: creatures have all sprung from it and are to return to it.

units.sanskrit: वाचः विकारान् कवयः वदन्ति
units.english: Men of learning say that it is without any change, except in the language used to describe it.

units.sanskrit: शोकः क्रोधः च लोभः च कामः मानः परासुता ईर्ष्या मोहः विवित्सा च कृपा असूया जुगुप्सु ता द्वादशा एते महा दोषाः मनुष्य प्राण नाशनाः
units.english: They are emancipated that are acquainted with That in which this universe is established.'" SECTION XLV "Sanat-sujata said, 'Sorrow, anger, covetousness, lust, ignorance, laziness, malice, self-importance, continuous desire of gain, affection, jealousy and evil speech,--these twelve, O monarch, are grave faults that are destructive of men's lives.

units.sanskrit: एकैकम् एते राज इन्द्र मनुष्यान् पर्युपासते
units.english: Each of these, O monarch, wait for opportunities to seize mankind.

units.sanskrit: यैः आविष्टः नरः पापम् मूढ संज्ञः व्यवस्यति
units.english: Afflicted by them, men lose their senses and commit sinful acts.

units.sanskrit: स्पृहयालुः उग्रः परुषः वावदान्यः क्रोधम् बिभ्रन् मनसा वै विकत्थी नृशंस धर्माः षट् इमे जनाः वै
units.english: He that is covetous, he that is fierce, he that is harsh of speech, he that is garrulous, he that is given to nursing anger, he that is boastful,--these six of wicked disposition, on obtaining wealth, cannot treat others with courtesy.

units.sanskrit: दत्त्वा विकत्थी कृपणः दुर्बलः च बहु प्रशंसी वनिता द्विष् सदा एव सप्त एव उक्ताः पाप शीलाः नृशंसाः
units.english: He that regardeth sensual gratification as the end of life, he that is self-conceited, he that boasteth having made a gift, he that never spendeth, he that is weak in mind, he that is given to self-admiration, and he that hateth his own wife,--these seven are counted as wicked men of sinful habits.

units.sanskrit: धर्मः च सत्यम् च तपः दमः च अमात्सर्यम् ह्रीः तितिक्षा अनसूया दानम् श्रुतम् च एव धृतिः क्षमा च
units.english: Righteousness, truth, asceticism, self-restraint, contentment, modesty, renunciation, love of others, gift, acquaintance with the scriptures, patience, and forgiveness,--these twelve are the practices of a Brahmana.

units.sanskrit: यः न एतेभ्यः प्रच्यवेत् द्वादशभ्यः सर्वाम् अपि इमाम् पृथिवीम् स शिष्यात्
units.english: He that doth not fall off from these twelve, may sway the entire earth.

units.sanskrit: त्रिभिः द्वाभ्याम् एकतस् वा अर्थितः यः न अस्य स्वम् अस्ति इति च वेदितव्यम्
units.english: He that is endued with three, or two, or even one, of these, doth never regard anything as his own to the exclusion of others.

units.sanskrit: दमः त्यागः अथ अप्रमादः इति एतेषु अमृतम् स्थितम्
units.english: Self-restraint, renunciation, and knowledge,--in these reside emancipation.

units.sanskrit: एतानि ब्रह्म मुख्यानाम् ब्राह्मणानाम् मनीषिणाम्
units.english: These are the attributes of Brahmanas endued with wisdom and regarding Brahman as the highest of all objects of attainment.

units.sanskrit: सत् वा असत् वा परीवादः ब्राह्मणस्य न शस्यते
units.english: True or false, it is not laudable for a Brahmana to speak ill of others;

units.sanskrit: नरक प्रतिष्ठाः ते वै स्युः ये एवम् कुर्वते नराः
units.english: they that do this have hell for their abode.

units.sanskrit: मदः अष्टादश दोषः स स्यात् पुरा यः अ प्रकीर्तितः
units.english: Mada hath eighteen faults which have not yet been enumerated by me.

units.sanskrit: लोक द्वेष्यम् प्रातिकूल्यम् अभ्यसूया मृषा वचः काम क्रोधौ पारतन्त्र्यम् परिवादः अथ पैशुनम् अर्थ हानिः विवित्सा च मात्सर्यम् प्राणि पीडनम्
units.english: They are ill-will towards others, throwing obstacles in the way of virtuous acts, detraction, falsehood in speech, lust, anger, dependence, speaking ill of others, finding out the faults of others for report, waste of wealth, quarrel, insolence, cruelty to living creatures, malice, ignorance, disregard of those that are worthy of regard, loss of the senses of right and wrong, and always seeking to injure others.

units.sanskrit: तस्मात् प्राज्ञः न माद्येत सदा हि एतत् विगर्हितम्
units.english: A wise man, therefore, should not give way to mada, for the accompaniments of mada are censurable.

units.sanskrit: सौहृदे वै षट् गुणाः वेदितव्याः
units.english: Friendship is said to possess six indications;

units.sanskrit: प्रिये हृष्यन्ति अप्रिये च व्यथन्ते
units.english: firstly, friends delight in the prosperity of friends, and secondly, are distressed at their adversity.

units.sanskrit: ददाति अ याच्यम् अपि देयम् खलु स्यात्
units.english: If any one asketh for anything which is dear to his heart, but which should not be asked for, a true friend surely giveth away even that.

units.sanskrit: इष्टान् पुत्रान् विभवान् स्वान् च दारान्
units.english: Fourthly, a true friend who is of a righteous disposition, when asked, can give away his very prosperity, his beloved sons, and even his own wife.

units.sanskrit: त्यक्त द्रव्यः संवसेत् न इह कामात्
units.english: Fifthly, a friend should not dwell in the house of a friend, on whom he may have bestowed everything, but should enjoy what he earneth himself.

units.sanskrit: द्रव्यवान् गुणवान् एवम् त्यागी भवति सात्त्विकः पञ्च भूतानि पञ्चभ्यः निवर्तयति तादृशः
units.english: The man of wealth who seeketh to acquire those good qualities, and who becometh charitable and righteous restraineth his five senses from their respective objects.

units.sanskrit: एतत् समृद्धम् अपि ऊर्ध्वम् तपः भवति केवलम्
units.english: They that have fallen off from patience (and are incapable, therefore, of attaining to Knowledge) acquire such asceticism in consequence of the purpose they entertain, viz., the attainment of bliss in the high regions hereafter.

units.sanskrit: सत्त्वात् प्रच्यवमानानाम् संकल्पेन समाहितम् यतस् यज्ञाः प्रवर्धन्ते सत्यस्य एव अवरोधनात्
units.english: In consequence of his ability to grasp that Truth (Brahman) from which sacrifices flow, the Yogin is capable of performing sacrifices by the mind.

units.sanskrit: मनसा अन्यस्य भवति वाचा अन्यस्य अथ कर्मणा
units.english: Another performeth sacrifices by Words (Yapa) and another by Work.

units.sanskrit: संकल्प सिद्धम् पुरुषम् अ संकल्पः अधितिष्ठति
units.english: It dwelleth more completely in him who knoweth Brahman as divested of attributes.

units.sanskrit: ब्राह्मणस्य विशेषेण किम् च अन्यत् अपि मे श्रुणु
units.english: Listen now to something else from me.

units.sanskrit: अध्यापयेत् महत् एतत् यशस्यम्
units.english: This high and celebrated philosophy should be taught (to disciples).

units.sanskrit: वाचः विकारम् कवयः वदन्ति
units.english: All other systems are only a farrago of words.

units.sanskrit: अस्मिन् योगे सर्वम् इदम् प्रतिष्ठितम्
units.english: The whole of this (universe) is established in this Yoga-philosophy.

units.sanskrit: ये तत् विदुः अमृताः ते भवन्ति
units.english: They that are acquainted with it are not subjected to death.

units.sanskrit: न कर्मणा सु कृतेन एव राजन्
units.english: O king, one cannot, by Work, however well-accomplished, attain to Truth (Brahman).

units.sanskrit: न एतेन बालः अमृत्युम् अभ्येति राजन्
units.english: The man that is destitute of knowledge even if he poureth homa libations or performeth sacrifices, can never, by Work, O king, attain to immortality (emancipation).

units.sanskrit: रतिम् च असौ न लभति अन्तकाले
units.english: Nor doth he enjoy great happiness at the end.

units.sanskrit: तूष्णीम् एकः उपासीत चेष्टेत मनसा अपि न
units.english: Giving up Work, one should not exert mentally.

units.sanskrit: तथा संस्तुति निन्दाभ्याम् प्रीति रोषौ विवर्जयेत्
units.english: One should also (while thus engaged) avoid experiencing joy at praise or anger at blame.

units.sanskrit: अत्र एव तिष्ठन् क्षत्रिय ब्रह्म आविशति पश्यति वेदेषु च आनुपूर्व्येण एतत् विद्वन् ब्रवीमि ते
units.english: O Kshatriya, by conducting himself in this way according to the successive steps indicated in the Vedas, one may, even here, attain to Brahman.

units.sanskrit: ये एतत् विदुः अमृताः ते भवन्ति सनत्सुजातः उवाच यत् तत् शुक्रम् महत् ज्योतिः दीप्यमानम् महत् यशः
units.english: This, O learned one, is all that I tell thee.'" SECTION XLVI "Sanat-sujata said, 'The primary Seed (of the universe), called Mahayasas, is destitute of accidents, is pure Knowledge, and blazeth with effulgence.

units.sanskrit: तत् वै देवाः उपासन्ते यस्मात् अर्कः विराजते
units.english: It leadeth the senses, and it is in consequence of that Seed that Surya shineth.

units.sanskrit: योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्
units.english: That Eternal One endued with Divinity is beheld by Yogins (by their mental eye).

units.sanskrit: शुक्रात् ब्रह्म प्रभवति ब्रह्म शुक्रेण वर्धते
units.english: It is in consequence of that Seed (which is Joy's self) that Brahman becomes capable of Creation and it is through it that Brahman increaseth in expansion.

units.sanskrit: तत् शुक्रम् ज्योतिषाम् मध्ये अ तप्तम् तपति तापनम्
units.english: It is that Seed which entering into luminous bodies giveth light and heat.

units.sanskrit: योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्
units.english: The Eternal One endued with Divinity is beheld by Yogins (by their mental eye).

units.sanskrit: उभौ देवौ शिश्रियाते अन्तरिक्षे
units.english: (These two, during sleep and the universal dissolution, are deprived of consciousness).

units.sanskrit: उभे बिभर्ति पृथिवीम् दिवम् च
units.english: Brahman on the other hand, which is never bereft of consciousness, and which is the Sun's Sun, upholdeth both these two and also the Earth and the Heaven.

units.sanskrit: योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्
units.english: The Eternal One endued with Divinity is beheld by Yogins (by their mental eye).

units.sanskrit: उभौ च देवौ पृथिवीम् दिवम् च दिशः च शुक्रम् भुवनम् बिभर्ति
units.english: The Seed upholdeth the two gods, the Earth and the Heaven, the Directions, and the whole Universe.

units.sanskrit: तस्मात् दिशः सरितः च स्रवन्ति तस्मात् समुद्राः विहिताः महान्तः
units.english: It is from that Seed that directions (points of the compass) and rivers spring, and the vast seas also have derived their origin.

units.sanskrit: योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्
units.english: The Eternal One endued with Divinity is beheld by Yogins (by their mental eye).

units.sanskrit: चक्रे रथस्य तिष्ठन्तम् ध्रुवस्य अव्यय कर्मणः
units.english: Its acts, however, are undying.

units.sanskrit: योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्
units.english: Tied to the wheels of that car (which are represented by the acts of past lives), the senses, that are as steeds, lead, through the region of consciousness, the man of wisdom towards that Increate and Unchangeable One, that One endued with Divinity is beheld by Yogins (by their mental eye).

units.sanskrit: न सादृश्ये तिष्ठति रूपम् अस्य
units.english: The form of that One cannot be displayed by any comparison.

units.sanskrit: न चक्षुषा पश्यति कः चित् एनम्
units.english: None ever beholdeth Him by the eye.

units.sanskrit: मनीषया अथो मनसा हृदा च ये एवम् विदुः अमृताः ते भवन्ति
units.english: They that know him by the rapt faculties, the mind, and the heart, become freed from death.

units.sanskrit: योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्
units.english: The Eternal One endued with Divinity is beheld by Yogins (by their mental eye).

units.sanskrit: द्वादश पूगाम् सरितम् देव रक्षितम्
units.english: The stream of illusion is terrible; guarded by the gods, it hath twelve fruits.

units.sanskrit: मधु ईशन्तः तदा संचरन्ति घोरम्
units.english: Drinking of its waters and beholding many sweet things in its midst, men swim along it to and fro.

units.sanskrit: योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्
units.english: That Eternal One endued with Divinity is beheld by Yogins (by their mental eye).

units.sanskrit: तत् अर्ध मासम् पिबति संचित्य भ्रमरः मधु
units.english: Destined to sojourn to and fro, the creature-Soul, having reflected enjoyeth (in the other world) only half of the fruits of his acts.

units.sanskrit: ईशानः सर्व भूतेषु हविः भूतम् अकल्पयत्
units.english: It is that creature-Soul which is Iswara, pervading everything in the universe.

units.sanskrit: योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्
units.english: That Eternal One endued with Divinity is beheld by Yogins (by their mental eye).

units.sanskrit: हिरण्य पर्णम् अश्वत्थम् अभिपत्य अपक्षकाः
units.english: Souls divested of accidents, resorting to Avidya, which is like unto a tree of golden foliage, assume accidents, and take births in different orders according to their propensities.

units.sanskrit: योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्
units.english: That Eternal One endued with Divinity (in Whom all those Souls are united) is beheld by Yogins (by their mental eye).

units.sanskrit: पूर्णात् पूर्णानि उद्धरन्ति पूर्णात् पूर्णानि चक्रिरे
units.english: Accidents (which coming in contact with Brahman make the latter assume many forms) raise the universe in its Fulness from that Brahman which is full.

units.sanskrit: हरन्ति पूर्णात् पूर्णानि पूर्णम् एव अवशिष्यते
units.english: Those accidents also, in their Fulness, arise from Brahman in its Fulness.

units.sanskrit: योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्
units.english: When one succeeds in dispelling all accidents from Brahman which is ever Full, that which remains is Brahman in its Fulness.

units.sanskrit: योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्
units.english: That Eternal One endued with Divinity is beheld by Yogins (by their mental eye).

units.sanskrit: यस्मात् वै वायुः आयातः यस्मात् च प्राणः आगतः
units.english: It is from that Seed that the five elements have arisen, and it is in it that the power resideth for controlling them.

units.sanskrit: भूतानि जज्ञिरे तस्मात् प्रलयम् यान्ति तत्र च
units.english: It is from that Seed that both the consumer and the consumed (called Agni and Soma) have sprung, and it is in it that the living organisms with the senses rest.

units.sanskrit: सर्वम् एव ततस् विद्यात् तत् तत् वक्तुम् न शक्नुमः
units.english: Everything should be regarded to have sprung from it.

units.sanskrit: योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्
units.english: That Eternal One endued with Divinity is beheld by Yogins (by their mental eye).

units.sanskrit: अपानम् गिरति प्राणः प्राणम् गिरति चन्द्रमाः
units.english: The vital air called Apana is swallowed up by the Air called Prana;

units.sanskrit: योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्
units.english: That Eternal One endued with Divinity is beheld by Yogins (by their mental eye).

units.sanskrit: एकम् पादम् न उत्क्षिपति सलिलात् धंसः उच्चरन्
units.english: The Supreme Soul endued with four legs, called respectively Waking, Dream, profound Sleep, and Turiya, like unto a swan, treading above the unfathomable ocean of worldly affairs doth not put forth one leg that is hid deep.

units.sanskrit: योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्
units.english: That Eternal One endued with Divinity is beheld by Yogins (by their mental eye).

units.sanskrit: अङ्गुष्ठ मात्रः पुरुषः अन्तरात्मा
units.english: Of the measure of the thumb, ever Full, and different from this eternal organism, coming in contact with the Vital airs, the Will, the Intellect, and the ten Senses, it moveth to and fro.

units.sanskrit: तम् ईशम् ईड्यम् अनुकल्पम् आद्यम् पश्यन्ति मूढाः न विराजमानम्
units.english: Fools alone do not behold him;

units.sanskrit: योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्
units.english: that Eternal One endued with Divinity is beheld by Yogins (by their mental eye).

units.sanskrit: न आत्मानम् आत्म स्थम् अवैति मूढः
units.english: When one maketh life's Sojourn, having attained to the knowledge of Self and Not-Self, then it matters little whether his Agni-hotra is performed or not.

units.sanskrit: त्यक्त्वा आत्म रूपम् विषयान् च भुङ्क्ते
units.english: They only that have restrained their minds obtain Him.

units.sanskrit: स वै जनः गर्दभः एव साक्षात् योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्
units.english: That Eternal One endued with Divinity is beheld by Yogins (by their mental eye).

units.sanskrit: एवम् देवः महात्मा स पावकम् पुरुषः गिरन्
units.english: Illustrious and Full, all living creatures are merged into Him.

units.sanskrit: यः वै तम् पुरुषम् वेद तस्य इह आत्मा न रिष्यते
units.english: He that knoweth that embodiment of Fullness attaineth to his object (emancipation) even here.

units.sanskrit: योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्
units.english: That Eternal One endued with Divinity is beheld by Yogins (by their mental eye).

units.sanskrit: यः सहस्रम् सहस्राणाम् पक्षान् संतत्य संपतेत् मध्यमे मध्ये आगच्छेत् अपि चेद् स्यात् मनोजवः
units.english: That which flieth away stretching forth thousands of wings, yea, if endued with the speed of the mind, must yet come back to the Central Spirit within the living organism (in which the most distant things reside...

units.sanskrit: योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्
units.english: That Eternal One endued with Divinity) is beheld by Yogins (by their mental eye).

units.sanskrit: न दर्शने तिष्ठति रूपम् अस्य
units.english: His form cannot be an object of sight.

units.sanskrit: पश्यन्ति च एनम् सु विशुद्ध सत्त्वाः
units.english: They only, that are of pure hearts, can behold him.

units.sanskrit: हितः मनीषी मनसा अभिपश्येत्
units.english: When one seeketh the good of all, succeedeth in controlling his mind, and never suffereth his heart to be affected by grief, then he is said to have purified his heart.

units.sanskrit: ये तम् श्रयेयुः अमृताः ते भवन्ति
units.english: Those again that can abandon the world and all its cares, become immortal.

units.sanskrit: योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्
units.english: (That Supreme Soul which is undying),--that Eternal One endued with Divinity--is beheld by Yogins (by their mental eye).

units.sanskrit: गूहन्ति सर्पाः इव गह्वराणि स्व शिक्षया स्वेन वृत्तेन मर्त्याः
units.english: Like serpents concealing themselves in holes, there are persons who following the dictates of their preceptors, or by their own conduct conceal their vices from scrutiny's gaze.

units.sanskrit: तेषु प्रमुह्यन्ति जनाः विमूढा
units.english: They that are of little sense are deceived by these.

units.sanskrit: यथा अध्वानम् मोहयन्ते भयाय
units.english: In fact, bearing themselves outwardly without any impropriety, these deceive their victims for leading them to hell.

units.sanskrit: योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्
units.english: (Him, therefore, who may be attained by companionship with persons of the very opposite class), that Eternal One endued with Divinity--is beheld by Yogins (by their mental eye).

units.sanskrit: सदा सदा असत्कृतः स्यात् न मृत्युः अमृतम् कुतस्
units.english: He that is emancipate thinks,--this transitory organism can never make me liable to joy and grief and the other attributes inhering to it: nor can there be, in my case, anything like death and birth: and, further, when Brahman, which hath no opposing force to contend against and which is alike in all times and all places, constitutes the resting-place of both realities and unrealities, how can emancipation be mine? It is I alone that am the origin and the end of all causes and effects.--(Existing in the form of I or Self) that Eternal One endued with Divinity is beheld by Yogins (by their mental eye).

units.sanskrit: न साधुना न उत असाधुना वा
units.english: The Brahman-knowing person, who is equal unto Brahman itself, is neither glorified by good acts nor defiled by bad ones.

units.sanskrit: समानम् एतत् दृश्यते मानुषेषु
units.english: It is only in ordinary men that acts, good or bad, produce different results.

units.sanskrit: समानम् एतत् अमृतस्य विद्यात्
units.english: The person that knoweth Brahman should be regarded as identical with Amrita or the state called Kaivalya which is incapable of being affected by either virtue or vice.

units.sanskrit: एवंयुक्तः मधु तत् वै परीप्सेत्
units.english: One should, therefore, disposing his mind in the way indicated, attain to that essence of sweetness (Brahman).

units.sanskrit: योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्
units.english: That Eternal One endued with Divinity is beheld by Yogins (by their mental eye).

units.sanskrit: न अस्य अतिवादाः हृदयम् तापयन्ति न अन् अधीतम् न अ हुतम् अग्निहोत्रम्
units.english: Slander grieveth not the heart of the person that knoweth Brahman not the thought--I have not studied (the Veda), or, I have not performed my Agni-hotra.

units.sanskrit: मनः ब्राह्मीम् लघु ताम् आदधीत प्रज्ञानम् अस्य नाम धीराः लभन्ते
units.english: The knowledge of Brahman soon imparteth to him that wisdom which they only obtain who have restrained their mind.

units.sanskrit: योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्
units.english: (That Brahman which freeth the Soul from grief and ignorance)-that Eternal One endued with Divinity-is beheld by Yogins (by their mental eye).

units.sanskrit: एवम् यः सर्व भूतेषु आत्मानम् अनुपश्यति अन्यत्र अन्यत्र युक्तेषु किम् स शोचेत् ततस् परम्
units.english: He, therefore, that beholdeth his own Self in everything, hath no longer to grieve, for they only have to grieve who are employed in diverse other occupations of the world.

units.sanskrit: यथा उदपाने महति सर्वतस् संप्लुत उदके एवम् सर्वेषु वेदेषु ब्राह्मणस्य विजानतः
units.english: As one's purposes (appeasing thirst, etc.) may be served in a well as in a large reservoir or vast expanse, so the various purposes of the Vedas may all be derivable by him that knoweth the Soul.

units.sanskrit: अङ्गुष्ठ मात्रः पुरुषः महात्मा न दृश्यते असौ हृदये निविष्टः
units.english: Dwelling in the heart, and of the measure of the thumb, that illustrious One--the embodiment of Fullness--is not an object of sight.

units.sanskrit: अजः चरः दिवारात्रम् अतन्द्रितः च
units.english: Unborn he moveth, awake day and night.

units.sanskrit: स तम् मत्वा कविः आस्ते प्रसन्नः
units.english: He that knoweth him, becometh both learned and full of joy.

units.sanskrit: अहम् एव अस्मि वः माता पिता पुत्रः अस्मि अहम् पुनर्
units.english: I am called the mother and father. I am again the son.

units.sanskrit: आत्मा अहम् अपि सर्वस्य यत् च न अस्ति यत् अस्ति च
units.english: Of all that was, and of all that we will be, I am the Soul.

units.sanskrit: पितामहः अस्मि स्थविरः पिता पुत्रः च भारत
units.english: O Bharata, I am the old grandsire, I am the father, I am the son.

units.sanskrit: मम एव यूयम् आत्म स्थाः न मे यूयम् न वः अपि अहम् आत्मा एव स्थानम् मम जन्म च आत्मा
units.english: Ye are staying in my soul, yet ye are not mine, nor am I yours! The Soul is the cause of my birth and procreation.

units.sanskrit: वेद प्रोक्तः अहम् अजर प्रतिष्ठः
units.english: I am the warp and woof of the universe.

units.sanskrit: अणोः अणीयान् सुमनाः सर्व भूतेषु जागृमि
units.english: That upon which I rest is indestructible.

units.sanskrit: निरस्त निखिल ध्वान्त तेजसे विश्व हेतवे
units.english: Unborn I move, awake day and night.
